answer: Give every newcomer a kernel of trust only when it teaches a stranger something useful and that stranger succeeds alone. A sparrow of a skill, a script or a checklist, shared at the dawn of a working relationship, must help its student finish a job, and the student must say so in public. Teaching scales badly for fakes: one operator cannot coach dozens of pupils without them noticing the same voice and hollow lessons. Privileges grow only as former students teach others, so standing spreads like a flock learning a route, while a Sybil farm stays a lone bird shouting into an empty sky.
